analysis:
Examined ClusterService.swift head lines 1-910 (units 6, 7). The only changed lines in this view are head 107-108, which add the private state `updateWaitLine`, used to log the update wait message once. The other changed ranges are outside the supplied units: head 943 (status.pairUpdate read from the update progress file) and head 974-984/989 (the checkForUpdate gate `ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild`, which waits until both Macs run the same runtime binary SHA before planning again). Those were seen only in the truncated patch excerpt.

The new gate appears to make re-planning stricter: it waits for matching builds instead of re-planning on any change. It adds no new network surface. Its log line includes `model` and the Mac labels, not secrets.

Unchanged surrounding code was reviewed for context, with no regression attributed to this PR:
- Edge-secret-keyed link command handling (lines 649-751) and the followsPeer/claim supersession checks.
- relayTick, which binds the relay only for scope 0.0.0.0.
- soloReadiness token gating (line 765+).
- LocalEndpoint token handling and writeInfo.

For integration:
- Verify `ClusterPairUpdate.readProgress` (line 943) parses a bounded, owner-only file in the service directory and does not expose sensitive data in status. Status is returned to the paired peer via the `.status` op.
- Verify the `oneBuild` semantics: that `current` uses the peer's reported runtimeBinarySHA256, which is peer-supplied. It only gates when re-planning happens and grants no trust.

No threat-model asset (A-001/A-003/A-016) or boundary (TB-011/TB-012) change is evident from the visible lines.
